question.problem:
The values of functions $q(x)$ and $r(x)$ and their derivatives at $x=4$ are given in the table below.

| $x$ | $q(x)$ | $r(x)$ | ${q}^{′}(x)$ | ${r}^{′}(x)$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $4$ | $-5$ | $3$ | $4$ | $-7$ |

Compute $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2q(x)+3r(x))$ at $x=4.$
question.worked_solution:
Using the sum and constant multiple rules, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2q(x)+3r(x))=2{q}^{′}(x)+3{r}^{′}(x).
$$

At the point where $x=4$, this gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2q(x)+3r(x))|}_{x=4} & =2{q}^{′}(4)+3{r}^{′}(4) \\  & =2\cdot 4+3\cdot (-7) \\  & =8-21 \\  & =-13.\end{aligned}
$$
